purpose: copied at the order of prince Raṇabahādura Sena
notes: The quoted colophon has no date. The catalogue gives [[SS]] 1186, which presumably comes from elsewhere in the manuscript. Read as Śaka 1186 it would be about 1264 CE, which does not fit a Sena prince with the Nepali-style name Raṇabahādura; the Sena princes of Makwanpur/Palpa date to the 17th–18th centuries. So the catalogue year may be misread or belong to another era; check it against the manuscript. The prince is not called king (rājakumāra), so he is not recorded as the reigning king. Antarvāṇi ('learned in scripture') is treated as an epithet or title of the scribe. The colophon calls the work 'bhāṣārasataraṃgaḥ' and describes it as 'bhāṣā ghaṭitam' (composed in the vernacular).
